QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_28

question.text: Kaplan-Schoar Public Market Equivalent (KS-PME) is used for:

answer.text: Benchmarking Cat I/II AIF performance against a listed market index by compounding cash flows at market returns
Calculating GST payable on management fees

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 9.7.5: KS-PME measures Cat I/II AIF performance relative to the listed market by using market index returns as the compounding factor on capital calls and distributions. KS-PME > 1 means AIF outperformed the market. The Trap: Options A, C, D are unrelated to performance benchmarking. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B touches on PME; XXI-B covers listed-market benchmarks more extensively. Manager's Pro-Tip: Pick the benchmark index thoughtfully — NIFTY50 for large-cap focused Cat II, NIFTY Midcap for mid-cap biased, or a custom sector-weighted basket. PPM should name the benchmark and the KS-PME methodology; changing benchmarks ex-post is not acceptable.
